prerequisites: Basic concepts of electromagnetic fields and waves

learning_outcomes.text: Manage the basic parameters and regulations on electromagnetic emissions of a radiating system.
Analyze the effects of reflection and transmission of electromagnetic waves and interpret their behavior.

Interpret the engineering parameters that define the elements composing a radio link according to the application, and, in particular, those of antennas, their value ranges and units, as well as their technical specifications (also in English).
Identify an antenna type, analyze its characteristics, frequency band, and applications.
Perform the balance of a link with basic propagation losses, interpret the propagation mechanisms associated with the environment and frequency bands, and use models to quantify them.
Analyze the specifications and parameters of specific components of a satellite link.
Identify and compare different satellite transmission systems based on orbit, applications, and services offered by organizations and consortia.
Understand the technical and regulatory fundamentals of frequency allocation, as well as be able to manage national and international frequency attribution tables.

syllabus_topics: Parameters of antennas, types of antennas and their characterization
Engineering parameters for the characterization of transmitter and receiver antennas (matching parameters, gain functions, polarization, EIRP, radiation performance, illumination efficiency)
Other types of antennas in wireless communications
Balance of a radio link in free space. Terrestrial propagation, characterization and models
Power balance of a free-space link
Characterization and specifications of link elements
Parameters related to signal-to-noise ratio, sensitivity, error probability, transmission speed and capacity, for evaluating reception in analog and digital radio links
Design of a radio link with reflection and obstacles
Effect of tropospheric refraction and equivalent rectilinear propagation
Ionospheric propagation: description and balance of an ionospheric link
Characteristics of multipath propagation and mobility; characterization parameters and operating criteria
Empirical and numerical models for propagation characterization and radio coverage calculation
Regulation on the use of the radio electric public domain and National Frequency Allocation Chart (CNAF)
Environmental impact of electromagnetic emissions: regulation of human exposure to electromagnetic emissions
Communication satellites. Orbits. Systems and applications. Satellite radio link
Examples of orbits associated with different missions and services; comparisons
Characterization of specific elements of the satellite link (onboard transponder, satellite antennas, transmitters, receivers and antennas in ground stations)
Link balance and specific loss factors

Some examples of configuration and specifications of satellite transmission systems (TV-SAT, broadcasting, V-SAT, telephony, internet, localization, navigation, security, earth observation and environmental applications)
Frequency bands, allocation to systems and services

assessment_methods.method: Practical work delivery and defense (Practical Block)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the final grade is calculated as (0.70 x T) + (0.3 x P), where T is the theoretical block exam score and P is the practical block score. A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in the theoretical block exam. If this minimum is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary examination, students may use the practical score (P) from the ordinary examination and a new written exam (T). A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required in the written exam; otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. Students can also opt for a single written exam covering the entire subject, whose score will directly be the final grade.
